# A CAD book that earns US dollars five times, at five awkward rates.
#
# Each earning is collected in one transaction stated in Canadian dollars: the
# US dollar bank takes the money and the revenue line states what it was worth
# that day, so each opens a cost basis on the bank at its own rate.
#
# The rates are the ones a bank publishes, at four decimal places, so what the
# dollars were worth lands on a Canadian cent only by chance. That is what makes
# each cost an awkward fraction rather than a round rate:
#
#     2,720.00 USD worth 3,771.28 CAD   ->  2773/2000
#     1,845.50 USD worth 2,530.55 CAD   ->  50611/36910
#     3,310.75 USD worth 4,642.66 CAD   ->  464266/331075
#       987.25 USD worth 1,341.77 CAD   ->  134177/98725
#     4,562.80 USD worth 6,473.70 CAD   ->  64737/45628
#
# Those denominators are in the tens of thousands and are not multiples of one
# another. While every basis is untouched they cost nothing to add up: a basis
# whose balance is still its own amount cancels the division and contributes
# exactly the money it came in for. Once part of a basis is spent the balance is
# no longer the amount, nothing cancels, and adding the terms takes the lowest
# common multiple of those denominators.
#
# `tests/research/how_big_a_summed_cost_basis_cost_gets_probe.py` measures both
# states and reports how many bits the total needs.
